samples.summary: Sibling structural commands (insertTable / deleteTable / applySpellSuggestion / insertImage / insertPageNumber) move the caret and rewrite blocks but never fire the cursor-move callbacks, so the same staleness this delta fixes for toggleList/indent/outdent persists there (and, worse, presence broadcasts a stale caret because the cursor really did move).
samples.evidence: `insertTable` (editor.ts:3302-3304) does `cursor.moveTo({ blockId: firstCellBlock.id, offset: 0 }); invalidateLayout(); render();` — `render()` is the plain layout+paint helper and does NOT call `afterCursorRender()` (only `renderWithScroll`/`renderCursorMove` at 2063-2078 do), and no `notifyStyleApplied()` is present. Same pattern in `deleteTable` (3331-3332, after `cursor.moveTo` at 3317/3328) and `applySpellSuggestion` (3180-3183). Consequence: the docs-view presence subscriber (packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-view.tsx:394) never learns the caret jumped into the new table cell, and the toolbar's Text-style/summary refresh (docs-formatting-toolbar.tsx:323) keeps reporting the previous block's type/style until an unrelated event fires. This is the exact defect class the delta's comment cites (#792); the delta covered the list paths and left the caret-moving structural paths uncovered.

samples.summary: indent()/outdent() now fire the cursor-move callbacks unconditionally, including on the pure no-op paths where every visited block hit a guard (`currentLevel >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL`, `currentLevel <= 0`, `marginLeft <= 0`) and nothing was mutated.
samples.evidence: indent (2894-2912) and outdent (2917-2934) `return` out of the per-block callback without writing anything when the level/margin is already clamped, yet `notifyStyleApplied()` runs afterwards regardless. Each such call re-runs every toolbar refresh callback and pushes a presence `updateCursorPos` (docs-view.tsx:394) for state that did not change. Harmless functionally (the callbacks are read-only), but it means holding Cmd+[ at level 0 emits a stream of spurious notifications; a `changed` flag around the loop, as `stepSelectionFontSizeImpl` (1082) already uses, would avoid it.
